answer: Value moves through copper conduits that wear with volume, so throughput is capped by age, and age is certified by a karst survey mapping how long the channel has dissolved. A mirror of each flow log is public, so duplicate channels show immediately. A new identity gets a thin conduit; widening it needs a survey, and the k-th survey an operator commissions costs k squared in copper, so n heads need about n cubed over three in surveys while waiting for karst age that cannot be rushed. Conduits cannot be sold, since a survey certifies the channel, not the owner.
